chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is incumbent upon the Muslims to strive in connecting with one another, to cooperate in showing sympathy, and to assist those in need, and for some to show sympathy to others, until they become as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded you: merciful among yourselves, mutually compassionate, and grieving for what is hidden from you of their affairs, just as the group of the Ansar used to be in the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical duties of Muslims towards each other according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes social cohesion as a religious duty, urging Muslims to emulate the Ansar's profound empathy during the Prophet's era. It highlights that true faith manifests in active mutual aid and shared emotional engagement, reflecting the Quranic ideal of believers being 'merciful among themselves.'
